headline: Postponed vote on $300,000 Project HOPE funding, advanced $1,400,000 bond for 103 Maine Avenue, and approved three special amusement permits.
summary: The Council heard public comments on homelessness, opioid funding, and the 103 Main Street property, then acted on routine items and new business. It postponed a vote on accepting MaineHousing funds for Project HOPE, gave first readings to several ordinances and resolves including a data center moratorium and a bond for land at 103 Maine Avenue, and approved three special amusement permits.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 24, 2026 Council meeting and the July 20, 2026 Business and Economic Development Committee meeting.
Passed Order 26-263 authorizing a municipal quitclaim deed for FALOON real estate at 28 William Street.
Passed Order 26-264 authorizing a municipal quitclaim deed for CARSON real estate at 70 Thatcher Street.
Passed Order 26-265 authorizing a municipal quitclaim deed for LEONARD real estate at 1579 Union Street.
Passed Order 26-266 authorizing a municipal bill of sale for real estate at 159 Holiday Park.
Passed Order 26-267 authorizing revisions to the Ambulance Service Policy, the Emergency Medical Services Transport Plan.
Passed Order 26-268 authorizing the City Manager to execute a temporary land lease for two lot locations to General Electric Company.
Passed Order 26-269 authorizing the City Manager to execute an agreement with Athena Health for electronic health record and medical billing services.
Gave first reading to Ordinance 26-270, a moratorium extension on data centers in the City of Bangor, Maine.

Gave first reading to Resolve 26-271 accepting and appropriating an Airport Improvement Grant of $5,534,795 from the FAA, $145,652.50 from MDOT, and $575,578.50 local match for taxiway rehabilitation.
Gave first reading to Resolve 26-272 appropriating $7,000 from Bangor Opioid Settlement Unspent Funds to the Together Place.
Gave first reading to Resolve 26-273 amending Council Resolve 26-195 for the total school budget for the Bangor School Department.

Gave first reading to Order 26-274 authorizing issuance of up to $1,400,000 of bonds to purchase land and improvements at 103 Maine Avenue, and referred it to the Finance Committee on September 21, 2026.

Postponed Resolve 26-253, accepting up to $300,000 from MaineHousing with a $126,000 match from Bangor Opioid Settlement Unspent Funds for Project HOPE, to the September 28, 2026 Council meeting, by a vote of 8-1.
Approved the Special Amusement Permit application of 81 Park Street LLC d/b/a The Tarratine, 81 Park Street.
Approved the Special Amusement Permit application of Giri Bangor Holiday Inc. d/b/a Holiday Inn, 404 Odlin Road.
Approved the Special Amusement Permit application of Las Palapas Mexican Restaurant, LLC d/b/a Las Palapas Mexican Restaurant, 8 Bangor Mall Boulevard.

MINUTES OF REGULAR MEETING BANGOR CITY COUNCIL- SEPTEMBER 14, 2026
Meeting called to order at 7:00 PM
Chaired by Council Chair Hawes
Councilors Absent: None
Meeting adjourned at 8: 29 PM
PROCLAMATION Proclaimed September as National Recovery Month
PUBLIC COMMENT KatieCoethankedtheCityCouncilfor theproclamationandalsofor supportingthe
bus service.
MikeFurrowspokeregardinghomelessnessandtheneedfor moreaccountability.
TeresaFallonfelt thehomelessproblemcouldbeaddressedwithoutdemonizingthe
peopleandthat intentionally instigating doesnothing to solvetheproblem. Shefelt
realistic pathways needed to be created for better outcomes.
SuzetteFurrow felt projects neededto go to other service centers as Bangor could not
handle what it has now.
ScottPardystatedtheroot of theproblem wasthe uncheckeddrug epidemicandthere
neededto be decisive structured intervention for fundamental change.
Phil Henry wantedan audit ofprogramsto showresultsandfull costs.
James Gallagher requested that City Councilors be seenin the downtown area.
JacquelineSmallwoodspokeregardingBanAir andtheneedfor appointmentof
committee members before the board proceeds anyfurther.
CatherineDevinedidn't wantmoneyto go toprojectsthat enableddrug useandfelt
the Council was not listening to the people.
Melissa Pelzawitz cautioned aboutforcing people into institutions as it was
unconstitutional as people have rights.
Beth Haggerty stated that everyone was in this together and needed to work together
for a solution.
Dr. Brian Calfman and Dr. Eric Wise asked the Council to reconsider their stance on
the Main Street property.
Jeff Forney questioned why the Council wanted the property at 103 Main Street and
askedthat the decisionto exercisethe City'sright offirst refusal bepostponeduntil a
cost/ benefit analysis could be conducted
